content.title: About
content.content: Soup, cream of mushroom is a thick, velvety soup made from fresh mushrooms, cream, broth and seasonings. It has a delicate mushroom aroma, smooth texture and a subtle creamy note.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mushrooms are one of the most widely consumed edible fungi worldwide.
Cream soups are often served in restaurants as a starter during colder months.
Traditional recipes use 10‑20% cream to achieve a silky consistency.
Mushroom soups contain aromatic compounds that enhance flavor perception.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Mushrooms provide niacin, riboflavin and vitamin B6, which support metabolism.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: The fiber in mushrooms aids normal digestion.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A serving of the soup contains about 120 kcal, making it suitable for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Selenium and ergothioneine in mushrooms help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports immune function
items.content: Beta‑glucans in mushrooms contribute to a stronger immune system.

items.title: Mushroom allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to mushrooms.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Using ready‑made broth can raise the salt level; adjust seasoning accordingly.

items.title: Dietary restrictions
items.content: People with kidney issues should limit mushroom intake due to purine content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the soup hot, often garnished with croutons, fresh herbs or a drizzle of olive oil. It can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and reheated on the stove.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared soup in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. It freezes well for up to 2 months. Reheat to a rolling boil before serving.
